learning: Iterations 5 and 6 showed that cutting yaw inertia through body_length lifted the s-bend (2 to 13 to 19 finishes) while the oval held 20 of 20. The slalom did not respond to either step. Mass is now the only remaining inertia lever, since body_length is at its minimum. If s-bend oscillation rises above about 0.35, the inertia limit has been reached for this controller, and the next gain should come from the controller.
notes: Iteration 7 package: the Builder's mass 0.5 kg step on the iteration 6 design (body_length 0.10). The controller is unchanged from iteration 6, so the only variable is yaw inertia.
rationale: Iteration 6 (score 657.9, the best raced design) shows that body_length 0.10 at mass 0.6 lifted the s-bend to 19 of 20 finishes, with line losses 0.55 and oscillation 0.33. The oval held 20 of 20 with max_error 0.017. The slalom is still at 0 of 20 finishes, with progress 0.26 and max_error at the 0.063 floor. It has not responded to any inertia change across iterations 5 and 6. The Builder's proposal lowers mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg with body_length held at 0.10 m, which cuts yaw inertia by about 17 percent (about 0.00122 to 0.00102 kg m^2). I accept the geometry as proposed, with every other value unchanged. For the controller I keep the iteration 6 gains exactly (kp 2.8, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.5, antisymmetric weights, last_direction), so any change in the race can be attributed to mass. The main risk is that s-bend steering_oscillation (0.33 at iteration 6, limit about 0.35) rises above the limit. If it does, the Builder's rule is to restore mass to 0.6 kg. Expected, not measured: s-bend finishes at 19 or 20 of 20 with line losses at or below 0.55, and the oval stays at 20 of 20.
